title: Compile-Time QoS Scheme for Deep Learning Inferences
problem: Accelerators (GPUs, TPUs, NPUs) increasingly shared for multiple concurrent deep learning inference services. Inference requests with sequences of short-duration kernels create challenges for online schedulers maintaining Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees with target latency requirements.
motivation: Inference workloads widely deployed for production services requiring strict latency SLAs. Online scheduling struggles with fine-grained kernel sequences. Compile-time approaches could eliminate scheduling burden by pre-determining resource partitioning.
method: QoSlicer breaks inference computations (kernels—tasks run on the GPU) into flexible pieces. Before running (at compile time), the system pre-computes multiple slicing plans and uses heuristic search to find which plan best meets each inference's latency target (maximum completion time). Performance estimation (test-run measurement) validates each plan will work. At runtime, the scheduler simply activates the right pre-computed plan, keeping decisions fast.
key_novelty: By pre-computing how to slice inference computations at compile time, QoSlicer guarantees latency targets without runtime scheduling overhead.
contributions: Compile-time kernel slicing framework for QoS guarantees
Heuristic search algorithm for optimal slicing plan generation
Robust performance estimation models validating plans against latency targets
20.2% average throughput improvement on 75 diverse workload combinations
limitations: Abstract-only; specific inference models, latency targets, and deployment scenarios not detailed.
